name: ANSI/IEEE current-measuring shunt symbol
summary: IEEE-oriented graphical reference for current-measuring shunt, with public vendor evidence and drawing-reading notes.
description: The shunt form identifies a resistive current path used to derive a voltage measurement. Power-current terminals and voltage-sense leads must be distinguished where the actual device provides separate sensing connections.

This is a convention-specific lookup based on the publisher's IEEE-labelled preview. The geometry here is independently drawn to explain the connection or operation; it is not a certified reproduction of the standard graphic.
readingNotes: Follow the sense circuit without confusing it with the full-current path.
Read the selected library and the project legend together. A vendor block identifier is meaningful within its named library and is not a universal standard-symbol code.
distinction: A shunt produces a measured voltage drop; a CT provides an instrument-transformer secondary current.
